'''''Encephalartos hirsutus''''' is a [[species]] of [[cycad]] that is native to [[Limpopo]] Province of [[South Africa]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tropicos.org/Name/100330594|title= Encephalartos hirsutus in Tropicos}}</ref> It was recorded from three separate localities on south-east-facing quartzite cliffs in the [[Makuya Nature Reserve]] bordering the [[Kruger National Park]] at elevations ranging from {{convert|800|–|1000|m|sp=us}} above sea level.<ref name="iucn" />

As of 2020, it is assumed there are up to 10 individuals in the wild.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Redlist article about the plant |url=https://www.iucnredlist.org/species/41889/51056445}}</ref>

==Description==
It is an arborescent cycad, with an erect stem, which becomes decumbent in older specimens, up to {{convert|4|m|abbr=on}} high and with a diameter of {{convert|35|–|40|cm|abbr=on}}. The leaves, pinnate, arranged in a crown at the apex of the stem, are {{convert|1.1|–|1.4|m|abbr=on}} long, supported by a petiole about {{convert|13|cm|abbr=on}} long, and composed of numerous pairs of elliptic leaflets and coriaceous, long {{convert|13|–|17|cm|abbr=on}}, with entire margin and thorny apex, fixed on the rachis with an angle of about 40°, reduced to thorns towards the base of the petiole. It is a dioecious species, with male specimens that have from 2 to 5 cylindrical-ovoid cones, erect, about {{convert|50|cm|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|9|cm|abbr=on}} broad, and female specimens with 1–3 ovoid cones, about {{convert|40|cm|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|35|cm|abbr=on}} broad, of glaucous green color, glabrous. The seeds are coarsely ovoid, {{convert|3|–|3.5|cm|abbr=on}} long, covered with an orange-red [[sarcotesta]].<ref name="Hurter Glen 1996 pp. 46–48">{{cite journal | last=Hurter | first=P.J.H. | last2=Glen | first2=H.F. | title=Encephalartos hirsutus (Zamiaceae): a newly described species from South Africa | journal=South African Journal of Botany | volume=62 | issue=1 | date=1996 | doi=10.1016/S0254-6299(15)30577-9 | pages=46–48| doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Threats ==
This species has effectively been extirpated in the wild due to over-collecting for ornamental purposes.<ref name=":0" />
